text:
mira: hitting AccessDenied on kms:Decrypt after a key rotation. app assumes role via STS then calls KMS. error: \"User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/redwood-app-role/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource\". Anyone seen this with conditional key policies?

josh: can you paste the key policy + the role ARN (mask acct id)? common culprit: MFA/Bool conditions or Principal referencing the original user.

mira: key policy snippet below (redacted):
```json
{
  \"Sid\": \"AllowAccount\",
  \"Effect\": \"Allow\",
  \"Principal\": {\"AWS\": \"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:root\"},
  \"Action\": \"kms:*\",
  \"Resource\": \"*\",
  \"Condition\": {\"Bool\": {\"aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent\": \"true\"}}
}
```

carmen: ahhh that Condition. When you assume a role via STS the session might not carry the MFA flag. Also the Principal: root block is too coarse — it doesn't explicitly allow the assumed role ARN. Key policy conditions are evaluated against the caller context.

mira: we rotated the key yesterday and turned on the MFA condition as a quick guard, didn't realize it would block our infra role. Is there a way to keep MFA for console users but let the role decrypt?

josh: two quick options: 1) explicitly add the role ARN as an allowed principal (e.g. \"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-app-role\") or 2) add a Condition that exempts the role, e.g. \"ForAnyValue:StringEquals\" on \"aws:PrincipalArn\". Example: 
```json
{\"Effect\":\"Allow\",\"Principal\":{\"AWS\":\"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-app-role\"},\"Action\":\"kms:Decrypt\",\"Resource\":\"*\"}
```

carmen: also check grants — if you issued a grant for a service principal it can bypass some policy checks, but grant tokens need to be provided during the STS flow. If your client doesn't include the GrantToken you'll still be denied.

mira: we don't use grants for this path, it's direct decrypt. ops logs show assume-role succeeded: `aws sts assume-role` -> got creds, then aws-kms Decrypt call fails.

sec-bot: KMS rotation completed for alias/aws/redwood-app at 2024-07-15T14:12:03Z — rotation id: rot-0abc123 (link)

josh: diagnostic steps: 1) assume the role locally and run `aws sts get-caller-identity` to confirm ARN. 2) run `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin --key-id alias/yourkey` with those creds. 3) if still denied, temporarily add an explicit Allow principal for the role and re-test.

mira: did `aws sts assume-role` + `aws sts get-caller-identity` — caller shows `arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/redwood-app-role/session-123`. added explicit key policy Allow for that role, redeployed, decrypt succeeded.

carmen: nice. follow-up: once you confirm, consider a least-privilege key policy that allows the role for specific actions (kms:Decrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey) and keeps the MFA Condition for interactive/root users. Example pattern: explicit Allow for role + default Deny with MFA for root users.

mira: will do. opened a quick PR to add the role principal + limited actions, and a note to ops to avoid turning on global MFA Condition without checking service principals. thanks all :thumbsup:

josh: if you want, we can add a guard in the infra runbook: when rotating keys, run the assume-role + decrypt smoke test in staging before enabling the condition.

mira: added to runbook. marking resolved. :white_check_mark:
